::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
China's largest OSAT (Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test) company and the world's third-largest — founded in 1972, now majority-owned via China Resources Microelectronics. Not found on the US Entity List in the sources checked for this tracker, despite advanced packaging increasingly being discussed as a future export-control target.
:::

**Chinese name:** 长电科技 (Chángdiàn Kējì)

## What does this facility make?

Chip assembly, test, and advanced packaging services — not a fab, but the step between a finished wafer and a sellable chip. Demonstrated high-volume packaging of 4nm-class chips using chiplet technology.

## Why does it matter?

Advanced packaging (chiplets, heterogeneous integration) is one of the segments China's Big Fund III and its OSAT majors are explicitly pivoting toward, since it offers a path to competitive chip performance without needing export-controlled leading-edge lithography.
